# Data inventory - every raw bench file in this repository

**Generated by `deliverables/2026-09-19-pause/analysis/code/build_inventory.py`.** Re-run it with

```bash
python3 deliverables/2026-09-19-pause/analysis/code/build_inventory.py
```

The machine-readable version is `data_inventory.csv` in this directory, with one row per file and
the same fields. **Nothing in `sessions/data/` was modified.**

## What is here

| | |
|---|---|
| Files inventoried | **165** across four session directories |
| Of those, raw data | **163** (78 `.csv`, 83 `.log`, 2 `.json`) |
| The rest | 2 transcribed console notes (`.md`) that are prose, not data |
| Scripts kept as provenance | **82** in the four `scripts/` directories |
| Files the session logs EXCLUDE from results | **24** |
| Files carrying a caveat that changes how they may be read | **65** |
| Empty files (zero bytes) | **5** |

> **A count to correct.** The brief for this work says 161 data files. The four directories hold
> **163** (78 `.csv` + 83 `.log` + 2 `.json`), plus 4 `README.md`, 2 transcribed console notes and
> 82 scripts: **251 files in total**. `SOURCE_INVENTORY.md`'s own per-directory numbers already sum
> to 163; only the brief's prose says 161.

## Where each file's settings came from

**Not one data file is missing its bias or its Z parking** - but for a fifth of them the setting is
not where a reader would look for it. This is the failure mode `CLAUDE.md` section 3b is about, and
it is worth naming because the answer was already in the repository every time.

| Where the bias had to be read from | Files |
|---|---|
| The session's data `README.md` or its session log - where you would look | **127** |
| **The producing script's own source**, committed in that session's `scripts/` directory | **18** |
| **The session log's code-changes section**, not the scan record - see the note below | **18** |
| **The data file's own printed banner** | **1** |
| **Not recorded anywhere** | **1** |

**The 2026-09-17 scans are the sharpest case.** Their bias is not written beside them anywhere. It is
recoverable because `sessions/2026-09-17-bench.md` records, in its code-changes section, that
`stm_feedback_scan.py` *"read a bias argument, printed it in its banner, and then ignored it - it
wrote `BIAS 38229` unconditionally... Every scan before that ran at -0.5 V whatever was typed"*.
The fix is commented at `Code/pc/stm_feedback_scan.py:206-211`. So **every 2026-09-17 scan was
taken at sample -0.5 V**, and the bug that made it so is also what makes it knowable. Credit for
finding it goes to the 2026-09-17 review team, who are named in that log.

**The one genuine gap** is `sessions/data/2026-09-18-bench/approach3.log`: `stm_approach.py` did not
set a bias at that date, so the sample sat at whatever the previous command left, and no document
says what that was. **UNKNOWN.**

## Files that carry a caveat

| File | Caveat |
|---|---|
| `2026-09-17-bench/diag_line_repeated.csv` | every fwd and back array is BYTE-IDENTICAL: the scratch tool stored the forward pass twice. Any trace-versus-retrace figure from this file is meaningless (sessions/2026-09-17-bench.md 3.25) |
| `2026-09-17-bench/line_repeated_wide.csv` | TWO things. (1) same byte-identical fwd/back defect as diag_line_repeated.csv. (2) its 636-count reproducible profile, carried as UNDETERMINED since 2026-09-17, is CLOSED: it is the feedback loop recovering from the 30,000-count X flyback between passes on a surface tilted at -0.105 Z counts per X count, which predicts a 3,144-count Z error at every pass start. Dropping two pixels of twenty-one takes the consecutive-pass correlation from +0.65 to +0.05. Found by subagent 2 at this pause point |
| `2026-09-17-bench/line_three_y_positions.csv` | the CORRECTION in 3.25 records that this control was run at the WRONG WIDTH (+-8000 against the wide scans' +-15000) and so had no power to discriminate. The +-15000 version of the same test WAS run and is scan_wide_25nm_1/2.csv in this directory - found 2026-09-19, and those two files had been missing from this directory's README table |
| `2026-09-18-bench/char1.csv` | every value is 32,767 - the ADC rail. It records a railed contact, not a measurement of current |

## Empty, truncated and header-only files

**Nothing in these four directories is corrupt.** Every `.csv` parses, every `.log` is readable text,
and both `.json` files load. What there is instead is files that are *short because the run was*
*short*, and the difference matters when a reader meets a two-row CSV.

| File | Bytes | What it means |
|---|---|---|

## What the scripts directories contain

| Session | Scripts | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `2026-09-17-bench` | **0** | **No scripts were kept for this session.** The scans came from `Code/pc/stm_feedback_scan.py` and from scratch variants of it that no longer exist. The diagnostic that stored the forward pass twice is one of those, and cannot now be inspected |
| `2026-09-18-bench` | 25 | Hardcode `COM3` and Jacob's Desktop path; **3** are `*_test.py` simulated-junction tests (`characterize_test.py`, `zcal3_test.py`, `fasttrack_test.py`), so 22 driving scripts share 3 tests |
| `2026-09-19-bench` | 37 | Same; **8** are `*_test.py` simulated-junction tests (`catch_and_scan_test.py`, `creeptrack_test.py`, `lift_test.py`, `live_backoff_test.py`, `live_touch_test.py`, `live_touch2_test.py`, `onset0_test.py`, `scan2_test.py`) |
| `2026-09-19-morning` | 20 | a different pattern: the test is INSIDE the script. 14 carry a working `--test` self-test on simulated junctions; **six do not** (`live_backoff_z0.py`, `zjump.py`, `where.py`, `passive_z0.py`, `touchtest.py`, `final.py`). All twenty refuse options they do not recognize |

**`scripts/final.py` was never run** - Jacob powered down first - so there is no tip-clear baseline
and no parked state recorded for the shutdown (`sessions/data/2026-09-19-morning/README.md`).
